text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
USCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
TaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 US presidential election.
∀x (USCitizenship(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
∀x (USCitizenship(x) ∨ TaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: A person either has US citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (RussianOfficial(x) ∧ TaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(Vladimir, Taiwanese) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬Manager(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is not a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ RussianOfficial(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
¬(CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∧ Participate(Vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register to vote and Vladimir can participate in the election.
